s1.syndrome_frame: asymptomatic solitary thoracic nodule with increased metabolic activity
salient_findings: 20-mm homogeneous, well-defined nodule in the right paratracheal region
no change in nodule size after 3 months
key_facts: 67-year-old man
undergoing evaluation for sigmoid colon cancer
contrast-enhanced CT showed a nodule in the right paratracheal region
FDG-PET showed increased uptake in the lesion
maximum SUV of 5.3
asymptomatic
unremarkable medical and family history
normal blood tests except for mild leukocytosis
laparoscopic sigmoidectomy performed
pathologic stage I sigmoid colon cancer
repeat CT 3 months later showed no change in nodule size

shortlist.label: Non-Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: High FDG uptake and solitary thoracic nodule

shortlist.label: Metastatic lung disease
shortlist.why_kept: History of sigmoid colon cancer and increased metabolic activity

shortlist.label: Sarcoidosis
shortlist.why_kept: Solitary thoracic nodule and mild leukocytosis

shortlist.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Solitary thoracic nodule and increased metabolic activity

shortlist.label: Adenocarcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Solitary thoracic nodule and history of cancer

raw.rationale: The high FDG uptake (SUV of 5.3) and the presence of a well-defined nodule in the right paratracheal region are consistent with malignant lymphoma, and given the patient's recent diagnosis of sigmoid colon cancer, the possibility of metastatic disease cannot be ruled out but the lack of change in nodule size after treatment of the primary cancer and the high SUV suggests a primary lymphoma process

rejected.label: Metastatic lung disease
rejected.why: lack of change in nodule size after treatment of the primary sigmoid colon cancer

rejected.label: Sarcoidosis
rejected.why: high FDG uptake and absence of other typical sarcoidosis findings

rejected.label: Hodgkin lymphoma
rejected.why: less common than non-Hodgkin lymphoma and no specific features suggestive of Hodgkin lymphoma

rejected.label: Adenocarcinoma
rejected.why: primary site not identified and less likely given the location and appearance of the nodule
